737: Part A – I am going through a difficult time. Recognising early changes in mood, body, thinking and relationships, and knowing when to ask for support.
740: What to look for in myself
743: Distress does not always show itself clearly
744: It often shows up through small changes in mood, body, thinking or relationships. It may begin with signs such as less patience, persistent tiredness, difficulty concentrating, a greater wish to withdraw or a feeling of not being able to stop.
745: Recognising early signs matters because people do not experience distress in the same way. Some become quieter or more distant; others, more irritable or reactive. In some people the impact shows mainly in the body, through tension, aches or fatigue; in others, it appears more in their thoughts, such as difficulty concentrating, repetitive thoughts or increased self-criticism.
746: More than identifying isolated symptoms, what matters is recognising changes in your own functioning. Simple questions can help:
747: Illustration: a tired person with drooping shoulders, next to an almost empty battery.
748: “Am I different from how I usually am?”
749: “Do I feel balanced, or am I just getting by?”
750: “Are these changes passing, or do they persist over time?”
753: Click on each area to see the signs and the reflection questions.
762: The emotional impact can show up in very different ways, not just as sadness or anxiety. You may notice:
764: Persistent sadness or difficulty feeling pleasure
765: Getting irritated easily, impatience or sharper replies
766: Feeling empty, apathetic or “emotionally switched off”
767: Frequent guilt, a feeling of failing or not being enough
768: Emotional ups and downs that are more intense than usual
